reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices Quarterly Progress Report: July 2025 - September 2025

description.narrative: The project identified 16 civic and governance challenges, of which 12 were successfully addressed, including infrastructure improvements, market operationalization, service delivery enhancements, and social accountability measures. Social media advocacy significantly contributed to these achievements. Capacity-building interventions strengthened youth understanding of democratic principles, legal frameworks, advocacy strategies, and digital engagement, while also empowering young persons with disabilities to navigate institutional barriers under the newly assented PWD Act 2025. SDG-focused activities linked local action to national and global development priorities. The program emphasized diversity, equity, and inclusion, ensuring accessible venues, gender-sensitive and age-appropriate approaches, and open-call participation to maximize equitable engagement. Strategic partnerships with political parties, civil society, and development partners facilitated cost-effective implementation, while deliberate anchoring of interventions within existing institutions ensured long-term sustainability and local ownership. Key lessons included the need for stronger inclusion of PWDs, enhanced SDG literacy at the grassroots, and culturally sensitive approaches to intergenerational dialogue. Moving forward, CMD Kenya will continue to strengthen capacity, expand government collaboration, and support youth and community-based organizations in translating dialogue into actionable advocacy and sustainable civic engagement.
